name: HTTP → AI Summary
description: Call an API and summarize the response with an AI/agent step.

config.prompt: Summarize the API response for an operator and suggest the next action: {{context.api.output.body}}

name: API → Transform → Tool
description: Fetch data, map outputs, and run a backend tool.

name: Human Approval Gate
description: Pause execution until a human approves the run.

name: Incident triage → GitHub + Slack
description: Webhook receives an incident, AI summarizes it, GitHub gets a tracking issue, Slack notifies the on-call channel.

config.prompt: You are an SRE assistant. Given this incident payload, write a 2-3 sentence summary suitable for a GitHub issue body. Payload: {{context.trigger.output}}

name: Customer escalation → Severity-routed response
description: Webhook receives a complaint, AI classifies severity, and condition-guarded edges fan out to one of three escalation branches: low (Slack ping), medium (GitHub issue + Slack), or high (human review + GitHub issue + urgent Slack alert).

complaint.description: The complaint text submitted by the customer

config.prompt: You are a customer-support triage assistant. Classify the severity of the following complaint as EXACTLY one lowercase word, no punctuation, no whitespace: `low` | `medium` | `high`. Use impact, urgency, and tone. Complaint: {{context.trigger.output.complaint}}

config.title: High-severity customer escalation
config.description: Review and confirm the response approach before the ticket is filed.

responseSummary.description: Short summary of how this will be addressed

owner.description: Slack handle or email of the responsible person

input.title: [HIGH] {{context.trigger.output.customer}}: customer escalation

name: Lead enrichment → sales handoff
description: Webhook receives a marketing-form lead, AI scores and enriches it, and a condition routes qualified leads to Slack + a welcome email while unqualified leads receive a nurture-sequence email.

teamSize.description: Self-reported team size; optional but boosts the qualification score

config.prompt: You are a sales qualification assistant. Score the following lead based on title seniority, company name, and team size. Respond with EXACTLY one lowercase word, no punctuation, no whitespace: `qualified` or `unqualified`. Lead: email={{context.trigger.output.email}}, company={{context.trigger.output.company}}, role={{context.trigger.output.role}}, teamSize={{context.trigger.output.teamSize}}

input.text: :dart: New qualified lead — {{context.trigger.output.email}} from {{context.trigger.output.company}} ({{context.trigger.output.role}}). AI rationale: {{context.score.output.response}}

input.subject: Welcome to Janusly — let's set up a quick call
input.text:
Hi {{context.trigger.output.company}} team,

Thanks for reaching out. We'd love to learn more about how you'd use Janusly. Reply to this thread and we'll get on a 15-minute call this week.

input.subject: Janusly for {{context.trigger.output.company}} — when you're ready
input.text:
Hi {{context.trigger.output.company}} team,

Thanks for your interest in Janusly. We've added you to our monthly product update; reply any time when the timing's right for a deeper look.

name: Refund triage → approval → billing webhook
description: Webhook receives a refund request, AI summarizes the claim, a human approval gate decides yes/no, then a signed webhook calls the billing system and an email confirms to the customer.

orderId.description: Original order id the refund applies to

config.prompt: You are a refund-triage assistant. Summarize the refund claim in 2 short sentences highlighting whether the reason sounds legitimate, any red flags, and the dollar impact. Claim: customer={{context.trigger.output.customer}}, order={{context.trigger.output.orderId}}, amountUsd={{context.trigger.output.amountUsd}}, reason={{context.trigger.output.reason}}

config.message:
Approve refund of ${{context.trigger.output.amountUsd}} for {{context.trigger.output.customer}} (order {{context.trigger.output.orderId}})?

AI analysis: {{context.analyze.output.response}}

input.subject: Your refund for order {{context.trigger.output.orderId}} has been processed
input.text:
Hi,

We processed your refund of ${{context.trigger.output.amountUsd}} for order {{context.trigger.output.orderId}}. It should hit your account within 5-10 business days.

Reply to this thread if anything looks off.

name: AI support draft → human review → send
description: Webhook receives a support ticket, AI drafts a response, a human agent reviews/edits via a typed form, and the final reply is emailed to the customer.

workflow.name: AI support draft → human review → send

config.prompt:
You are a customer support agent for Janusly. Write a polite, factual reply to the following ticket. Keep it under 200 words. Do NOT invent product features. Ticket subject: {{context.trigger.output.subject}}

Customer asked: {{context.trigger.output.question}}

config.title: Review the AI-drafted reply before sending
config.description: Edit the body if needed and approve to send to the customer.

finalBody.description: Final reply body. Pre-filled from the AI draft; edit as needed.

tone.description: Optional tone tag (warm | direct | apologetic) for analytics

name: Churn-risk weekly digest (scheduled)
description: Cron-fires every Monday 9am, pulls at-risk users from a configured analytics endpoint, AI ranks them, then a digest message lands in Slack for the customer-success channel.

config.prompt: You are a customer-success analyst. Given this at-risk-user payload, rank the top 5 customers by churn likelihood and write a one-line action for each. Keep the whole reply under 1000 chars. Payload: {{context.fetch_signals.output.body}}

name: Email auto-reply
description: Skeleton for reading inbound email and sending a templated reply via email.send. Operator fills the trigger source and recipient details in the Inspector.

input.subject: Auto-reply
input.text: Thanks for your message — I'll get back to you shortly.

name: Failed workflow recovery → DLQ → patch → replay
description: Headline recovery demo. A webhook fires a write-side billing call that is intentionally broken in two ways: no approval gate upstream of the write, and a Bearer token referencing an unbound secret. The run lands in the Recovery Queue; the AI suggests both an upstream approval insertion (structural) and a swap_secret_ref fix (config). One demo, two recovery patterns.

workflow.name: Failed workflow recovery → DLQ → patch → replay

input.subject: Your charge for ${{context.trigger.output.amountUsd}}
input.text:
Hi,

We processed your charge of ${{context.trigger.output.amountUsd}}. Reply if anything looks off.

name: Monthly metrics report → PDF → email
description: Scheduled cron fires on the first of each month, fetches metrics from an analytics endpoint, AI summarizes the top movers, pdf.generate renders a polished PDF, and email.send delivers it. Showcases schedule + http + ai + pdf + email in a single workflow — the operations / finance buyer's favorite.

config.prompt: You are a business analyst. Given this monthly metrics payload, write a 3-paragraph executive summary covering: top movers, anomalies worth investigating, and a recommended next action. Keep the whole reply under 800 chars. Payload: {{context.fetch_metrics.output.body}}

input.subject: Monthly metrics report

name: Multi-agent decision support (debate + arbiter)
description: Webhook receives a decision prompt, three sequential agents debate the proposal — an optimist supports it, a skeptic critiques it, and an arbiter weighs both sides and writes the final recommendation. Showcases the multi_agent primitive — orchestration that Zapier and n8n cannot reproduce.

proposal.description: The decision or proposal to debate

config.goal: Decide whether to approve the proposal: {{context.trigger.output.proposal}}

agents.name: optimist
agents.goal: List the three strongest arguments FOR this proposal: {{context.trigger.output.proposal}}

agents.name: skeptic
agents.goal: List the three strongest arguments AGAINST this proposal, given the optimist already argued for it. Proposal: {{context.trigger.output.proposal}}

agents.name: arbiter
agents.goal: Weigh the optimist's and skeptic's arguments and write a 3-sentence final recommendation (approve / reject / needs more info). Proposal: {{context.trigger.output.proposal}}

input.subject: Decision recommendation: {{context.trigger.output.proposal}}

name: MCP Notion → AI summary → Slack
description: Webhook receives a Notion page id, calls an external MCP server (alias notion-demo) to read the page, AI summarizes the contents, and Slack notifies the team. Showcases Janusly as an MCP client — operators wire a Notion MCP connection once in the admin MCP panel, then any workflow can consume it.

config.prompt: Summarize this Notion page in 3-5 bullets, focused on action items and decisions. Page content: {{context.read_page.output.result}}

name: Bulk customer classify → digest email
description: Webhook receives a batch of customers, the loop primitive normalizes each one into a summary line, AI classifies the entire batch in a single grouped call, and email.send delivers the digest. Showcases the loop primitive for fan-out aggregation and the scale-tier story.

name: Invoice intake → AI check → approval → accounting
description: A webhook receives a vendor invoice, AI flags anomalies (duplicates, unusual amounts), a human approves payment, then a signed webhook posts it to the accounting system and the vendor gets a confirmation email.

workflow.name: Invoice intake → AI check → approval → accounting

lineSummary.description: Optional one-line summary of the line items

config.prompt: You are an accounts-payable assistant. Review this invoice for red flags: possible duplicate, amount unusual for the vendor, due date already past, or vague line items. Answer in 2 short sentences ending with RISK: low, medium, or high. Invoice: vendor={{context.trigger.output.vendor}}, invoiceId={{context.trigger.output.invoiceId}}, amountUsd={{context.trigger.output.amountUsd}}, dueDate={{context.trigger.output.dueDate}}, lines={{context.trigger.output.lineSummary}}

config.message:
Approve payment of ${{context.trigger.output.amountUsd}} to {{context.trigger.output.vendor}} (invoice {{context.trigger.output.invoiceId}}, due {{context.trigger.output.dueDate}})?

AI check: {{context.check.output.response}}

input.subject: Invoice {{context.trigger.output.invoiceId}} approved for payment
input.text:
Hello,

Invoice {{context.trigger.output.invoiceId}} for ${{context.trigger.output.amountUsd}} was approved and scheduled for payment by {{context.trigger.output.dueDate}}.

Reply to this thread if anything looks off.

name: New-hire kickoff → IT access + team welcome
description: A webhook announces a new hire, AI drafts a role-aware welcome and access checklist, then a GitHub issue tracks IT provisioning, Slack announces the start, and the new hire gets a welcome email.

workflow.name: New-hire kickoff → IT access + team welcome

role.description: Role or team, e.g. Backend Engineer

config.prompt: You are a people-ops assistant. For a new {{context.trigger.output.role}} starting {{context.trigger.output.startDate}}, write (1) a 3-5 item IT/access checklist appropriate for the role and (2) a warm two-sentence welcome note addressed to {{context.trigger.output.name}}. Label the sections CHECKLIST and WELCOME.

input.subject: Welcome to the team, {{context.trigger.output.name}}!
